title: Questions, class and small talk (Fragen und Smalltalk)
summary: Where the verb goes in statements and questions, the verb haben, and the phrases you need in a class and in a first chat.
goals: Put the verb in the right place: second in statements and W-questions, first in yes/no questions
Ask for help in class: repeat, explain, spell
Keep a short small talk going

nicosWeg.title: Nicos Weg A1, chapter 1: Meeting people (Woher kommst du?)

sections.title: Where the verb goes
sections.text:
This is the most important rule of German word order:

- **Statements:** the verb is in **second** place: [[Ich wohne in München.]] Even when something else comes first: [[In München wohne ich.]]
- **W-questions** (wer, was, wo, woher, wie): question word first, verb second: [[Wo wohnst du?]]
- **Yes/no questions:** the verb comes **first**: [[Wohnst du in München?]] - [[Ja.]] / [[Nein.]]

Russian makes a yes/no question just with the voice (Ты живёшь в Мюнхене?), and Armenian with the voice and the ՞ mark. German normally moves the verb to the front instead: [[Wohnst du in München?]]

And unlike Armenian, the verb never waits until the end of a simple sentence: [[Ich lerne heute Deutsch.]]
[[du hast]] and [[er hat]] lose the b. [[haben]] and [[sein]] are the two verbs you will use most; it pays to know both tables by heart.

items.de: Wie sagt man das auf Deutsch?
items.en: How do you say that in German?

items.de: Wie lange wohnst du schon in München?
items.en: How long have you been living in Munich?
items.note: German uses the present tense here.

sections.text: [[Wie lange wohnst du schon in München?]] uses the present tense for something that started in the past and still goes on, exactly like Russian (Я живу здесь год) and Armenian. English needs 'have been living'; German and your languages don't.
[[gern]] after the verb means you like doing it: [[Ich lerne gern Deutsch.]] = I like learning German. [[Ich arbeite gern hier.]] = I like working here.

items.explanation: Yes/no question: the verb comes first.
W-question: question word first, verb second.

items.hint: Yes/no question, and the first word of a sentence starts with a capital letter.
items.explanation: Hast du eine Frage? The verb comes first, and du hast loses the b.
